title: Human Factors / Minimum Complement Evaluations
metaDescription: Minimum-complement determination sized to protective-strategy requirements, with human-factors and fatigue considerations built into the analysis.
heroDek: The right staffing number is a calculation, not a headcount someone remembers from years ago. GSS sizes minimum complement to the response strategy, with fatigue and shift-pattern effects built in rather than assumed away.
contextHeading: The right number of people is a calculation, not a headcount someone remembers
contextParagraphs: Minimum complement is the smallest protective-force staffing level that can execute the response strategy across every shift and posture. It is derived from the response positions and force allocation the timeline analysis requires, not from whatever the site has traditionally staffed.

Human factors are built into that calculation, not treated as a separate concern layered on afterward. Shift rotation, fatigue, and cognitive-load effects are evaluated directly, because a complement that is numerically sufficient but chronically fatigued will not actually perform to the timeline it was sized against.

The determination is re-run whenever the underlying protective strategy, staffing model, or facility configuration changes, and results are documented to support both staffing decisions and licensing-basis submissions.

methodology.label: Response Requirement Review
methodology.body: Response positions and force allocation drawn from the response strategy.

methodology.label: Task & Workload Analysis
methodology.body: Duties, concurrent-task demands, and shift coverage requirements analyzed per position.

methodology.label: Fatigue & Shift-Pattern Evaluation
methodology.body: Shift rotation and fatigue factors evaluated against sustained performance requirements.

methodology.label: Complement Calculation
methodology.body: Minimum staffing level calculated to cover all positions and postures across the full schedule.

methodology.label: Sensitivity Testing
methodology.body: Complement tested against absence, leave, and contingency scenarios.

methodology.label: Documentation & Basis Support
methodology.body: Findings documented to support staffing and licensing-basis decisions.

faq.q: Is minimum complement just the smallest number that satisfies regulation?
faq.a: No. It's sized to what the response strategy actually requires, with human-factors margin built in, not set at a bare regulatory floor.

faq.q: How often should this be re-evaluated?
faq.a: Whenever the protective strategy, staffing model, or facility configuration changes, rather than treated as fixed once determined.

faq.q: Does fatigue really change the calculated number?
faq.a: Yes. Sustained-performance and shift-pattern effects are built directly into the calculation, not addressed as a separate policy question afterward.
